newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds see dollars and sterling, Mexico in lira.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds see dollars and sterling, Mexico in lira.

text.p: The primary market saw a string of major deals on Thursday, with the European Investment Bank, British Telecom and Mexico coming to the market.
The EIB issued the first sterling bond which can be redenominated into euros when the single currency is introduced.

A syndicate manager at one of the co-leads said while the pricing was on the generous side for the EIB, initial take-up was on the slow side. "The redenomination clause has confused rather than enthused the sterling boys," he said.
Elsewhere, British Telecom added $500 million to its recent five-year offering bringing the total size to $1.5 billion.
The new paper was reoffered 12 basis points over U.S. Treasuries. The deal was originally launched at a 15 b.p. spread on April 8 and had since tightened to eight b.p.
On the emerging market side Mexico issued its expected 500 billion lire 20-year bond via Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
An official there said the deal had been well-received by Italian investors, and the issue was part of Mexico's strategy to diversify its funding away from dollars, marks and yen.

"Mexico plans to tap a variety of European currencies ahead of monetary union and this issue was part of its strategy to make sure European investors know its story and are familiar with the credit," the Deutsche syndicate manager said.

The lack of high-yielding paper in the lira bond market has boosted demand for emerging market deals, bankers said, with Argentina and Brazil also planning bonds in the coming weeks. Mexico was able to pay 80 b.p. less for the lira bonds relative to where its dollar paper is trading, they said.
Ecuador's long-awaited debut bond was expected to surface soon, possibly even later on Thursday, dealers said, and could total up to $400 million. Chase is lead manager of the issue.
Ecuador will issue a two-part global debt offering consisting of a five-year fixed rate issue and a seven-year floating rate note, a source close to the deal said in New York.
The five-year fixed rate issue is expected to yield 475 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes, but there was no price talk for the seven-year floater, dealers said.
